observations: A white-outlined oval form sits against a solid black ground, its interior packed with overlapping loops of yellow, blue, red, and purple line work that reads as dense cross-hatched scribble.

Two eye-like forms near center-left differ in treatment: the left carries a spiral with yellow and black surround, the right is a black-filled shape with yellow interior and a red outline above it, the two connected by a thick red angular bracket.
A secondary cluster of red and black curling forms breaks out of the oval at lower right, sitting partly outside the white boundary on the black ground.
reading: The oval boundary holds a crowd of competing marks without resolving them into calm. Dense looping lines fill the interior, while the two eye-like forms pull focus through contrasting colors and outlines. The red bracket linking them reads as tension rather than symmetry. The lower-right cluster, spilling past the white edge, suggests the form is under pressure from within.
